title: The agent runtime client has no published operation, no call type and no target-side home for the record write
source: Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5, TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T-A.1 and T3.1-T3.3; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8, 11, 16 and 41-44; Ownership Map v1 (api rows for P10 rwb-agent, P3 rwb-case and P7 rwb-decision); legacy story RWB-TE-013 sections 3, 4, 8, 12 and 13; Template and Rules v1 §R4, §R5.5 DP-02, DP-03, DP-04, DP-11, DP-13 and DP-20
section: s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 2 and 9; s8 BR8; s12.1 REST operations provided; s13 Configuration and reference data; s15 Screens and states
description: The legacy client is a Java interface inside one deployment: AgentStepClient.runStep with AgentStepRequest, RuleResult and AgentStepOutcome, an AgentOrchestrator.run call in the same JVM, a P7 DecisionLogWriter of the same process and a Quartz job step of RWB-TE-007. The target needs four things no source states. First, the seam: the eleven P10 operations of TSD P10 v2 T-A.1 hold no run-submit operation and no run-to-record link, so the step operation and the link operation, their paths and their request and answer members must be named by the story. Second, the call type between a calling step and rwb-agent: Arch v5 slide 16 shows AgentRunWorkflow on queue rwb-agent, DP-11 and DP-20 make the in-process call a REST contract with a fake, and no source says which of the two the seam uses or how a repeat that arrives while the first run is RUNNING is answered. Third, the budget: DP-11 fixes one hop with a 2 s client budget while agent_policy.timeout_seconds is 60 (R-UNI-32) and NFR-010 allows 60 seconds for an answer. Fourth, the identities and the small value sets: the per-service login of rwb-agent is not named, the guardrail check-code list that carries the legacy value SCHEMA is not a list in TSD P10 v2 T3.2, and the record write is split between the local library of the caller and the run of the agent service with only DP-03 to settle it. The route path of the run read behind gateway-bff is also unnamed.
evidence: TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T-A.1 lists eleven operations with no POST /agent-runs and no decision-record link; legacy RWB-TE-013 section 12 gives the Java interface only; Architecture v5 slide 16 'AgentRunWorkflow: 60 s, then rule result'; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-11 'REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout' against DP-20 'rwb-agent contract'; legacy section 3 names SY-CASEWF, SY-AGENT and SY-DECLOG but no service login; TSD P10 v2 T3.2 lists LOV-AUTONOMY, LOV-AGENT and LOV-PRODUCT but no check-code list.
proposed: Publish the two operations and their members in the rwb-agent contract baseline of RWB-P10-TE013-CON, record the 60 s budget as the single exception to DP-11 in ADR-020, name the rwb-agent login with the wave 1 schemas, and settle the guardrail check-code list with RWB-P10-E1058-APP before the story is Done.

title: The client contract has no source member types, refusal detail or record reference shape
source: Recovery Workbench API Specification v4.yaml (P10 paths); TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T-A.1, T3.1 and T3.3; Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 (DF-AGT-058, DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018); legacy story RWB-TE-013 section 12; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-03, DP-11 and DP-13; RWB-P10-E1058-CON (platform error envelope)
section: s3 Preconditions; s7 AC1 and AC6; s11 Data; s12.1 REST operations provided; s12.8 Contract fakes
description: The contract slice must fix the JSON spelling and the types of members the legacy story gives as Java records: ruleResult as a record of ruleId, ruleVersion, toState and a JsonNode result, inputs as an untyped map, confidence as a float and the record reference as a UUID. No source states the JSON shape of a free-JSON member, the decimal scale of confidence, the detail text of a refusal, or which identifier the record reference carries at the seam, although DF-AGT-058 is a CROSS_REF uuid and rwb-decision owns the record type and the ledger. The refusal set of the step operation also has no source: the legacy interface throws one exception, R-UNI-40 fixes the repeat rule, and the platform uses status codes, so 401, 403, 409, 422 and 503 are the contract's reading rather than a quoted rule. The gateway-bff route in front of the run read is unnamed in every source.
evidence: Legacy RWB-TE-013 section 12: record AgentStepOutcome(UUID decisionLogEntryId, RuleResult appliedResult, JsonNode recommendation, boolean fallback, String fallbackReason, String autonomyMode, UUID agentRunId); TSD P10 v2 T-A.1 gives the eleven operations with their refusal sets but no run-submit operation; TSD P10 v2 T3.3 joins the run and the record by ID only; no source gives the record reference type at the boundary, the JSON shape of ruleResult.result, or the route path of the agent admin read.
proposed: Fix the member names and their JSON spelling in the contract and leave the types to the review with the owners of rwb-decision and rwb-case; settle the refusal set and the record reference with the same review, and name the route when the edge contract RWB-PLT-N001-CON is baselined.

title: The release has no source topology, sizing, login name, alert threshold, runbook text or route path
source: Recovery Workbench Non Functional Specification v3; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T6.2 and T7; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8, 11, 20, 41 and 44; Ownership Map v1 (P10 rows); legacy story RWB-TE-013 sections 2, 5, 13, 14 and 15; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-02, DP-10, DP-17 and DP-19
section: s3 Preconditions; s7 AC1, AC5 and AC6; s10 Authority; s11 Data; s13 Alert mapping and Capacity; s15 Screens and states; s19 Out of scope
description: The deployment slice must state a chart, a migration job, a worker registration, a publish right, a feature switch, probes, dashboards, alerts, a runbook, a rollback and a capacity plan. No source gives the deployment topology detail (cluster names, node pools, replica counts, resource sizes, zone spread, ingress class, probe paths and timings), the host, the SKU or the budget; the per-service login of rwb-agent has no name and no secret name; the alert thresholds, the evaluation windows and the runbook wording are absent although the legacy story fixes the 10 percent fallback target and the MSG-P7-003 condition; and the gateway-bff route path in front of the run read is unnamed in the edge contract. The release also has to show that no Quartz job window and no lake window remain, which follows from §R6 and DP-17 rather than from any deployment source.
evidence: TSD P10 v2 T7 gives targets, not sizing; Architecture v5 slide 20 and slide 41 name the namespace rwb-recovery and one queue per service but no chart values; legacy RWB-TE-013 section 2 gives the fallback target 'below 10 percent per month' and section 5 the MSG-P7-003 condition, with no threshold, window or runbook text; DP-02 requires one login per service and no source names it; DP-19 requires the route and no source names its path.
proposed: Carry every environment value as a chart value with a reviewed copy per environment, reference the login through a platform secret, draft the five alert rules and the six runbook entries for sign-off by the on-call rota, and publish the route from the edge contract when it is baselined.
